preview: Interview experience of Parth Shirole for an internship at SAP Labs, detailing the coding round, two technical interviews, and the HR round.
content: Interview Experience Parth Shirole, B.Tech Comps 2020-2024 Eligibility Criteria: 70 % or 7 CGPA and above in current graduating degree and 60% in 10th & 12th Coding Round Date: 4th August 2022 Question 1: We were given a 2D matrix of integers. We needed to return an array where the i'th element of the array corresponds to the maximum integer in the i'th row of the given matrix. Example - Matrix = [[1, 2, 3], [4, -9, 8], [11, 3, 19]] Output = [3, 8, 19] Question 2: An array was given to us and another integer k was provided. We needed to sort the first k elements of the array in ascending order and rest of the elements in the descending order. Example: Array = [2, 6, 9, 23, 0, -1, 4, 9, 5] and k = 5 Output: [0, 2, 6, 9, 23, 9, 5, 4, -1] Overall the coding round was very easy. We had been given a total of 1 hour to attempt these 2 questions. However I submitted the test in 15 minutes itself as all my test cases had passed. Technical Interview I Date: 9th August 2022 Time: Around 10 AM Around 40 students were shortlisted for this round ●The interview started off with the interviewer asking for my introduction. I told him about my hobbies and interests and then gave a brief about the kind of projects I had done ●Since I had worked on MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas on a hackathon project, he asked what issues I faced and how me and my team solved it. He further asked if I knew what DDOS is and what measures I had taken to prevent it from happening to my website ●Next, he asked me "What can I ask you?". Here I made the mistake of being overconfident and I said "Anything". He started asking me about load balancing and sharding which I wasn't really sure about. When I couldn't answer these questions properly, he again asked me the same question. And this time I replied with DBMS. ●From DBMS, I was asked - Difference between RDBMS and DBMS, examples of each, types of joins. I was also asked to combine columns from 3 different tables using a common attribute. ●What is data lake and data ocean? I wasn’t very sure about this ●Trick question - I was asked how can I select all columns from a table. To which I replied using SELECT * FROM tablename. He then said, he uses ‘@’ for selections like these as it's more efficient. I said I haven’t heard of this before and then he admitted this was just a trick question. Technical Interview II Date: 9th August 2022 Time: Around 4PM Around 28 students were shortlisted for this round. ●This time I wasn’t asked to introduce myself but was asked about one of my projects ●Asked me the approach for solving https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/count-ways-reach-nth-stair-using-step-1-2-3/ I mentioned recursion and explained how I would implement this. I wasn’t asked to code this. ●Asked me the time complexity of the code snippet - for(int i=1; i < n; i *= k) ●I was asked how would I delete a node from linked list when the pointer is already at that node. Even though this question was easy, I could only solve it after getting a hint from him. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/in-a-linked-list-given-only-a-pointer-to-a-node-to-be-deleted-in-a-singly-linked-list-how-do-you-delete-it/ ●I was asked to open my desired code editor (I chose vs code of course) and code the below question in 5 min https://www.javatpoint.com/program-to-find-the-frequency-of-characters The one mistake I made here was I accidentally defined char as int. This ended up printing the ascii codes of the character instead of the character itself. But I spotted this instantly and fixed it. ●The final question I was asked was a puzzle - https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-7-3-bulbs-and-3-switches/ Thankfully, I was already aware of this puzzle and how to solve this. He only gave me 2 minutes to answer this question. So I pretended to think a little and then answered it easily. HR Round Date: 9th August 2022 Time: Around 6:30 PM 9 people were shortlisted for this round. This round was more relaxed and the HR was also very polite. She asked me what my hobbies were and was I tired from the whole day of interviews. She asked why I wanted to join SAP. Since I had attended their pre-placement talk, I knew what principles they worked on and what they valued the most. Hence I said the answer somewhat along those lines and the HR seemed satisfied. The round barely lasted 5 minutes The HR round was the final round and results came in at around 10PM on the same day. All 9 students who had qualified for the HR round were also shortlisted for the internship position at SAP Labs.
